subject: Mutual Action Plan: performance evaluation & close timeline
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@nimbusai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:15:00 +0000
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: performance evaluation & close timeline

Tom —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion I drafted a short Mutual Action Plan (attached) so both teams have a shared evaluation scope and a proposed close timeline. High-level asks we heard from Nimbus: EU data residency, sustained concurrency testing ~200–300 concurrent sessions, and a target P95 latency you called out (<=200ms for gen workloads).

Proposed MAP highlights (see attached MAP_Draft_v1.pdf):
- Evaluation metrics: latency (p50/p95/p99), sustained throughput (TPS), TTFT (time to first token), cold-start behavior, and variance under bursts.
- Modes to test: Hosted API (shared), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), Private (VPC/on-prem prototype).
- Isolation checks: noisy-neighbor sensitivity, tail-latency under mixed workloads.
- Autoscaling behavior: warm-up time, scale-up latency, and steady-state throughput per node.
- Acceptance criteria: P95 latency <=200ms or documented QoE tradeoffs; predictable throughput for 95% of the test window.

Suggested schedule:
- Week 1 (this week): finalize MAP and access (API keys, VPC peering request).
- Week 2: provisioning of dedicated test pool + Private deployment (short-lived infra).
- Week 3: run sequential experiments (Hosted baseline -> Dedicated -> Private) and collect traces + token-level latency.
- Week 4: review results, product/CS recommendations, and close decision (contract/commit).

Next steps I propose: 1) confirm the test windows you prefer, 2) share any region/network constraints (IPs to whitelist), and 3) confirm who from Nimbus will own security/compliance checklist.

I attached the MAP draft and a quick Test Matrix template we can fill together.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short working session if helpful.

—
Marcus Lin

Marcus —

Thanks, this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side before you spin up resources:
- Region: EU only (primary: eu-west-1). Data residency is a hard requirement.
- Peak concurrency: nominal 200 concurrent sessions, spike up to ~300 for 10–15 minute bursts.
- Workloads: short chat-style prompts (avg 80 tokens request, 200 token response) and a small set of heavy-generation prompts (single long response flows to 1k tokens).
- Acceptance thresholds: P95 <= 200ms preferred, P99 <= 400ms acceptable with documented tradeoffs.

We will need a Dedicated test environment for one of the runs — we want to validate isolation under noisy neighbors and confirm autoscale behavior. Also attaching our internal requirements XLS (network/firewall, credential rotation, SOC checklist).

We are targeting an internal procurement decision by 1 May 2027; if testing completes and satisfies the acceptance criteria we would move to finalize contract terms that week.

Subject: RE: Mutual Action Plan: performance evaluation & close timeline — results summary

Tom / team —

We ran the agreed experiments and pulled together a short results summary below. Full artifacts (traces, dashboards, and raw CSV exports) are available at the HubSpot/Drive links I included in metadata. High-level findings:

1) Hosted (shared API) — baseline
- p50: 85ms, p95: 220ms, p99: 410ms
- Sustained throughput observed: ~120 TPS (short-chat workload)
- TTFT: median 45ms; observed increased variance during multi-tenant bursts
- Notes: good median latency but tail sensitivity under concurrent spikes; autoscaling for shared tier is conservative (cooldown to avoid oscillation) which increased tail for short bursts.

2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, eu-west-1) — isolation & predictability
- p50: 70ms, p95: 160ms, p99: 280ms
- Sustained throughput observed: ~500 TPS (batched short-chat workload); long-gen throughput ~110 TPS for 1k token flows
- TTFT: median 40ms, very stable across windows
- Autoscaling behavior: scale-up ~90–120s to add capacity under scripted ramp; steady-state stable with low variance
- Notes: clear improvement in tail and throughput vs Hosted; isolation prevented noisy-neighbor regressions seen in Hosted runs.

3) Private (VPC in Nimbus account) — best isolation, slightly different scaling profile
- p50: 68ms, p95: 150ms, p99: 260ms
- Sustained throughput: ~520 TPS (short-chat); long-gen throughput similar to Dedicated
- TTFT: median 38ms
- Autoscaling behavior: scale-up slightly longer (~2–3 minutes) because of cluster autoscaler interactions in customer VPC; but once warmed, predictability and isolation were excellent
- Notes: lowest tail latency and best isolation; additional ops coordination required for certificate rotation and network egress rules.

Interpretation and recommended next steps:
- If Nimbus values tight tail-latency guarantees and isolation for regulatory/SLAs, Dedicated or Private both meet the P95 <=200ms goal easily.
- Hosted is acceptable for median-latency use cases but will require either guardrails (ingestion throttles) or a move to Dedicated for predictable tail behavior under your spike profiles.
- Autoscaling tradeoff: Dedicated hits the sweet spot for predictable scale and quicker scale-up vs Private (which has slightly longer scale-up due to customer infra).

Proposed close timeline (per your procurement window):
- Week of 26 Apr: finalize configuration and contract terms (pricing for Dedicated commitment vs Private onboarding).
- 1 May: target procurement decision.
- Early May: begin production onboarding and final runbook handoff if contract is signed.

Next step from us: I'll send a short pricing/options sheet that maps Dedicated commit sizing to expected unit costs and a PS estimate for Private onboarding. Lauren/Jordan/Priyom will be available for a 30-minute readout with your infra team to review the artifacts and answer any security questions.

—
